The Serie A clash between Inter and Verona on May 17, 2026, provided a masterclass in tactical discipline and late-game unpredictability. The match unfolded as a classic encounter between a dominant force and a resilient underdog, keeping fans on the edge of their seats until the very last whistle. Nerazzurri Dominance and the Opening Breakthrough From the outset, Inter established a stranglehold on the match, commanding a staggering 75% of ball possession. Petar Sucic was the focal point of their creative efforts, delivering a relentless series of corners that tested the Verona backline. While the first half remained goalless despite the pressure—with Yann Sommer comfortably handling headers from Nicolas Valentini and Sandi Lovric —the deadlock was finally broken in the 47th minute. An unfortunate own goal by Andrias Edmundsson gave Inter the lead they had been searching for, setting the stage for what seemed like a routine victory. Stoppage Time Twists and Turns As the clock ticked down, Inter introduced fresh legs, including Piotr Zielinski and Federico Dimarco , while Raffaele Di Gennaro replaced Sommer in goal. The hosts nearly doubled their lead in the 86th minute when a goal-bound shot from Petar Sucic was heroically hacked off the line by the Verona defense. This goal-line clearance proved to be a turning point, as it kept the visitors within striking distance. In the first minute of added time, the narrative shifted dramatically. Kieron Bowie found space in the box and unleashed a left-footed strike that found the back of the net, leveling the score at 1-1. Verona even threatened a late winner through Ioan Vermesan , whose header flashed wide, but the final whistle confirmed a dramatic draw that felt like a victory for the visitors and a missed opportunity for the dominant hosts.

The Allianz Stadium played host to a tense Serie A encounter on May 3, 2026 , as two sides looked to secure vital points in the league standings. Both teams brought high intensity to the pitch, knowing that every tactical decision and individual moment of brilliance could define their season's trajectory. Lightning Start in Turin Juventus wasted no time establishing dominance, stunning their opponents with a goal in the opening minute of play. Andrea Cambiaso provided a pinpoint assist for Dusan Vlahovic , who clinicaly finished with his left foot to give the home side an immediate lead. The pressure continued to mount, and just four minutes later, Chico Conceicao came inches away from doubling the advantage, but his strike rattled the post and stayed out. The first half was characterized by Juventus controlling 65% of the ball and creating numerous opportunities. Gleison Bremer even attempted an audacious bicycle kick in the 22nd minute that flew wide, while Kenan Yildiz and Conceicao kept the Lecce defense busy with a series of dangerous corner deliveries. Despite the pressure, the visitors managed to stay within reach as the match progressed into a tactical battle. VAR Drama and Defensive Resilience The second half turned into a frustrating affair for the Bianconeri as they battled both the Lecce defense and the technology. Twice the stadium erupted as Juventus appeared to have found a second goal—first in the 49th minute and again in the 61st—only for VAR to intervene and rule both strikes out for offside. Dusan Vlahovic found himself frequently caught by the visitors' offside trap, leading to a stop-start rhythm that kept the result in the balance. As the clock ticked down, tactical substitutions saw Federico Gatti , Jonathan David , and Edon Zhegrova enter the fray to help see out the result. Lecce attempted to find an equalizer late on, with Lassana Coulibaly sending an effort wide, but Juventus remained composed. In the dying seconds, Wladimiro Falcone produced two vital saves to deny David and Zhegrova , ensuring that while the scoreline remained narrow, Juventus walked away with all three points.

Sandi Lovric sent multiple deliveries into the box, and a late header from Nicolas Valentini forced a sharp save from goalkeeper Jean Butez .
